channel.title: HSJ - Latest news
channel.description: Custom RSS feed for HSJ latest news

item.title: Private providers face tougher rules on payment
item.description: A major government review into the prevalence of mental illness and neurodivergence is set to call for a mandatory tariff and specification to tackle huge variation in price and quality in ADHD and autism services, HSJ understands.

item.title: Six ‘neighbourhoods’ seek investors to ‘de-risk’ expansion
item.description: Six “neighbourhood health” projects are being pump-primed by government to secure millions of pounds of private investment.

item.title: Exclusive: NHS CEO will keep top-tier status
item.description: The NHS chief executive is set to have equal rank in government to the health department’s permanent secretary when NHS England is abolished – meaning a proposal to downgrade their status has been rejected by ministers.

item.title: Managers ‘should not feel affronted’ by Letby inquiry, says CEO
item.description: No NHS leader “should feel affronted” at being reminded of basic duties towards patients by the Letby inquiry, the chief executive of the Countess of Chester Hospital Foundation Trust has said.

item.title: FT takes over services from failing provider
item.description: A trust has completed an unprecedented takeover of services from a failing independent provider.

item.title: £2.5bn tech programme dubbed ‘unachievable’
item.description: Successful delivery of NHS England’s £2.5bn Frontline Productivity programme “appears to be unachievable” due to governance failures and political uncertainty, according to a government review.

item.title: Former midwife to chair merger trust
item.description: A former nursing and midwifery leader has been chosen as the first chair of a trust being created through merger next year.

item.title: Embarrassing Thirlwall is wrong about NHS management
item.description: The Thirlwall inquiry may be of some use to the families involved, but its summary findings and recommendations are patronising, confusing and in some cases plain ignorant, says HSJ editor Alastair McLellan.

item.title: Boards must ‘never again treat baby safety as side issue’, says Cooper
item.description: Maternity and neonatal services “cannot operate on the margins,” and deaths of babies and children must be investigated as a priority by NHS boards, the health and social care secretary has warned.

item.title: Inquiry chief delivers scathing verdict on NHS managers
item.description: Too many managers do not meet the standards expected of them, and there is an “urgent” need to improve quality, a major inquiry has found.

item.title: Tougher sanctions on senior managers demanded by Letby inquiry
item.description: The government must introduce a statutory barring system for managers by September next year, an inquiry has said – but warned it will only work if trusts are more willing to confront serious misconduct.

item.title: Cooper appoints ‘strong and capable’ CQC chair
item.description: The health secretary has named Baroness Julia Neuberger as the Care Quality Commission’s new chair, after MPs said they believed she would be “strong and capable”.

item.title: Grasp ‘politically unpopular’ mergers or face more deaths
item.description: Politically unpopular and “very difficult” decisions are required to tackle rising maternal death rates and improve safety, a leading academic has warned.

item.title: EPR launch delayed by eight months
item.description: An acute trust has delayed the full go-live of a new electronic patient record by eight months after a data problem, and to avoid launching in winter.

item.title: Dead bodies exposed to view from public footpath
item.description: A body being prepared for release in a hospital mortuary was visible from a publicly accessible footpath through a fire exit door propped open in hot weather, inspectors have found.

item.title: NHSE increases value of ‘tiger teams’ EPR contract
item.description: A consultancy firm will net an additional £6.4m over the next six months from its “tiger teams” contract with NHS England.

item.title: Hospital groups are falling out of fashion
item.description: Just under a year ago, HSJ reported that nearly two in five trusts shared a chair and/or chief executive – and that this represented significant growth over the previous 12 months.

item.title: Chair of £3bn trust to step down
item.description: The chair of a £3bn hospital trust will step down at the end of the year, after a decade spent leading some of the NHS’s top organisations.

item.title: Exclusive: First AI clinical negligence claims lodged
item.description: The NHS has received its first clinical negligence claims related to the use of artificial intelligence, HSJ can reveal.

item.title: NHSE’s FDP claims face fresh investigation
item.description: NHS England is being investigated again by the statistics regulator after a trust revealed it did not write a case study highlighting the local benefits of the FDP.
